To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) diffusive bistable arrays with weak diffraction are very different than dispersive bistable arrays with Kerr nonlinearities; (2) focusing nonlinearity is more desirable than defocusing nonlinearity; and (3) the packing density of optical arrays with diffusive bistability can be estimated using the reduced map, and is much higher for self-focusing nonlinearity than for self-defocusing nonlinarity.

the bistability of a Fabry-Perot cavity with self-focusing nonlinearity is stronger, with wider hysteresis, than with self-defocussing nonlinearity, that optical arrays with self-focusing nonlinearities can be more densely packed, and that a reduced map can predict the behavior of optical arrays and bistable cavities with self-focusing and self-defocusssing nonlinearity.
diffusive bistable arrays with focusing nonlinearities have wider hysteresis and wider operation gaps than with defocusing nonlinearity and that they allow finer packing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diffraction, focusing nonlinearities, and strong diffusion on bistable responses of Fabrey–Perot cavites and optical memory.
the effects of diffraction and diffusion on bistable optical arrays.
the effects of diffraction on diffusive optical bistability and optical memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diffusive bistable array with self-focusing nonlinearity is the best optical memory.
the effects of diffraction are to weaken the nonlinear response of optical arrays and optical bistable devices.
the presence of strong diffusion, weak diffraction, and Kerr nonlinearity can lead to bistable optical arrays with improved response characteristics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

diffraction and diffusion can be used as an effective tool to control the nonlinear behavior of an optical array, in a way that is similar to the use of nonlinearity to control the behavior of a dispersive system.
, for bistable optical arrays, the best choice is focusing nonlinearity, and the best choice for optical memory is defocusing nonlinearity.
, with self-defocusing nonlinearities and strong diffraction, the optical array is not a good memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, with focusing nonlinearities, bistable optical arrays can be designed to operate at much higher packing densities, which are of interest for all-optical memory.
the diffusive bistability model is very different than dispersive bistable optical systems.
, with weak diffraction and self-focusing nonlinearity (or self-defocusing non-linearity with stronger diffraction), optical bistability can be enhanced.
